summary: char-ai-sdk ships import-time obfuscated payload with sandbox-detection native addon
details: Package advertised as an AI SDK (persona/memory/Bedrock/OpenAI) ships four large obfuscator.io-style blobs at the package root — cache-warm.mjs (~280 KB), cache-sweep.mjs (~298 KB), build-cache.mjs (~204 KB), workspaces.js (~290 KB) — each disguised with an identical 'Auto-generated by char-ai-sdk@1.0.0 - build cache manifest' header followed by a base64/XOR-encoded `_0x<hex>` string array. These files are listed in package.json `files` and are reached on import: the main entrypoint re-exports from personas.mjs, which top-level imports./cache-warm.mjs, so requiring or importing the package unconditionally executes the opaque decoder and payload. In addition, native/<platform>/<arch>/cache-probe.node is a prebuilt N-API addon exporting VMDetect/VMDetectWorker that enumerates hypervisor, QEMU, VirtualBox, Docker, Podman, WSL, Bluestacks, AMD-SEV, SMBIOS/DMI, chassis, MAC, firmware and PCI signals; the filename misdescribes its contents and the capability is unrelated to the SDK's advertised purpose. The clean SDK code lives under dist/ and does not reference the obfuscated blobs or the VM-detect addon. The combination — import-time execution of a hex-identifier obfuscated blob behind a cover comment, co-shipped with a sandbox/VM-detection native binary — is the standard dropper + anti-analysis shape and provides arbitrary code execution on installer machines on `npm install` followed by any require/import of the package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
